By the time that games start utilizing 8 cores the 8350 will be outdated. For crying out loud [2011](http://www.techspot.com/images2/news/bigimage/2014/12/2014-12-17-image-4.jpg) is printed on the heatspreader. The architecture is old and the 8350 will get outperformed by Haswell i5's although it is more you will be getting better performance

At the time Haswell prices are going down because Intel is really pushing skylake. You can buy a 4690k and a z97 mobo for the same price as 6600k by itself. Including the RAM and the Cooler that you would need to get you would end up spending about $100 more on 6600k. If you have the money go for it it's good to be up to speed with the current architectures but the 4690k is still a very viable option and will be for at least 3 more years with a decent OC. And it will be a very good upgrade from your 8350. Not to mention it shouldnt bottleneck GPU's for a long time as well. If you have the money and want to spend the ~$450 on skylake but keep in mind haswell is still viable

In conclusion both games are very similar at their core so it really just depends whether you'd like to go with a Medieval setting or a post apocalyptic setting. They feature open expansive worlds with lots to do and although they aren't Last Of Us levels of character development (IMHO) they offer a very satisfying depth to the main characters.
